lead.headline: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil's president; Bolsonaro rejects result
lead.dek: Final tally gives Lula 51.8% and a margin of nearly 4.4 million votes; senator seeks to annul the vote
body: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a nonconsecutive fourth term Sunday with 51.8% of the runoff vote over right-wing Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, who refused to concede and said he would seek annulment after polling hours were extended.

The final count gave Lula a margin of nearly 4.4 million votes, The Associated Press reported, reversing the Oct. 4 first round, in which Bolsonaro led 47% to 45%. Justice Cristiano Zanin extended voting by two hours at both campaigns' request, but some polling stations had already shut down their voting machines and could not reopen, and Bolsonaro called the result "inexplicable."

Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, takes office Jan. 5 as the first candidate since democracy returned in 1989 to lose a first round and win the runoff. Bolsonaro, 45, had pledged to pardon his father, ex-President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving 27 years for plotting a coup. Federal police are investigating election-day transport disruptions in five states, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters.

briefs.headline: Appeals judges question DOJ suit over California ballots
briefs.summary: A 9th Circuit panel pressed a DOJ lawyer Sunday on its bid to sequester ballots of about 20,000 voters it calls likely noncitizens; a district judge hears the case Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Fire at Oregon seafood plant forces 1-mile evacuation
briefs.summary: A freezer fire at Pacific Seafood's Newport plant Sunday prompted evacuations over ammonia fears; officials later said there was no contamination risk and no injuries.

briefs.headline: U.S. measles cases top 4,580, double last year's total
briefs.summary: CDC data shows more than 4,580 cases this year, 96% among people unvaccinated or of unknown status; Pennsylvania reports 1,338 cases and five deaths.

briefs.headline: Home sellers cut prices as mortgage rates hit 7.4%
briefs.summary: The median listing price fell 1.2% from a year earlier to $419,250 in September, an 11th straight monthly decline, Realtor.com said; 21% of listings took a price cut.

briefs.headline: Vucic concedes as Serbia's Student List wins snap election
briefs.summary: Aleksandar Vucic said "it is clear that we have lost" and estimated the Student List would win 135 to 140 of 250 seats to his list's 105. Turnout was 64.9% by 6 p.m., the highest since 1992; final results are pending.

briefs.headline: Jordan arrests three suspects in church attack that killed 9
briefs.summary: Security forces took the three men from an abandoned house in Karak governorate after they fired on the raid, spokesman Mohammad al-Momani said. Friday's attack on a funeral at Hamoud church killed nine and injured 25.

briefs.headline: China's Central Committee opens four-day plenum on party discipline
briefs.summary: About 300 members met in Beijing on Monday to take up a draft decision on "full and rigorous party self-governance," Xinhua said. Eight committee seats are vacant and 15 members are under investigation.

briefs.headline: Attackers kill nurse responding to Ebola alert in eastern Congo
briefs.summary: WHO said the nurse was killed and a second health worker seriously injured Saturday in Bafwasende, Tshopo province. Congo's health ministry counts more than 9,800 cases and 4,700 deaths in the outbreak since May.

briefs.headline: PSC opens six days of hearings on MARL power line
briefs.summary: Evidentiary hearings on NextEra's 107.5-mile, 500-kilovolt Mid-Atlantic Resiliency Link begin Monday in Charleston and run through next Monday, with about 190 intervenors; nearly 59 miles would cross four northern counties.

briefs.headline: Logan County plans procession for deputy killed Saturday
briefs.summary: An on-duty deputy died Saturday afternoon when his cruiser and a coal truck collided at Route 10 and Rum Creek Road, the sheriff's office said. His name has not been released; a procession leaves Charleston about 5 p.m. Monday for Man.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court gives state until Nov. 20 in school funding case
briefs.summary: Justices extended the state's deadline, from Oct. 30, to respond to the ACLU-WV suit calling the school aid formula inadequate. Berkeley County schools gave 30-day notice last week of their own funding lawsuit.

briefs.headline: US 35 paving in Putnam County begins Monday
briefs.summary: Crews will mill and repave a 1.2-mile stretch between Hurricane Creek Road and Five and Twenty Mile Bridge, closing the northbound slow lane and cutting the speed limit to 50 mph. Phase one is due to finish in December, the DOT said.

regional.item: Huntington City Council votes Monday on a $182,607 contract for slip repair on 5th Avenue in Guyandotte.
One person died in an early Saturday house fire near Clendenin; the state Fire Marshal's Office is investigating.
Memorial Health System signed the final beam Friday on the 16-bed Sistersville General Hospital, due to open in 2027.

away.item: Bennington's Select Board hears the proposed local option tax at 6:30 tonight and a regional EMS consolidation plan at 7:45.

hotspots.item: Addison's building commission voted Oct. 14 to suspend Garage Strong, a youth training gym on Main Street, over fire-safety and insurance concerns, the Echo reported.
Surf City holds an open house on its updated bike and pedestrian plan Thursday, Oct. 29, 6 to 8 p.m., at the municipal complex, WECT reported.

briefs.headline: Bond calls NDP result 'devastating' as final count nears
briefs.summary: Former BC United MLA Shirley Bond said David Eby will regret the snap call and that Doerkson is the most northern premier since Dan Miller in 1999. Elections BC's final count runs Nov. 6-10; Return Day is Nov. 18.

briefs.headline: Cougars drop fourth straight at home in 3-2 loss to Tri-City
briefs.summary: Grady Martin scored twice in 2:15 of the third period Saturday before 5,554 at CN Centre to complete the Americans' weekend sweep. Prince George went 0-4 on the homestand and sits last in the Western Conference at 3-7-0-1.

briefs.headline: Doerkson names transition chief, leaves fall sitting open
briefs.summary: Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said Sunday he has spoken with the lieutenant-governor and named former deputy minister Kim Henderson to chair his transition. He did not rule out a fall sitting; no swearing-in date is set.

briefs.headline: 1,200 Teck workers strike at Highland Valley Copper mine
briefs.summary: United Steelworkers Local 7619 walked out Saturday at the mine near Logan Lake after contract talks failed; Teck said operations continue at reduced capacity. The union said 944 members voted unanimously for a strike mandate.

briefs.headline: First Nations chiefs meet Carney and premiers in Ottawa
briefs.summary: Monday's closed-door meeting is the first of its kind since the 2005 Kelowna Accord talks. Alberta's Danielle Smith and Quebec's Paul St-Pierre Plamondon said they would not attend; Manitoba's Wab Kinew joined Sunday's ceremony.

briefs.headline: IUCN finds 96% of assessed reefs critically endangered
briefs.summary: An assessment by the IUCN, the University of Melbourne and more than 250 researchers found all 17 Australian reef ecosystems at risk of collapse by 2075.

briefs.headline: Astronomers simulate universe's first 2 billion years
briefs.summary: Researchers at the Center for Astrophysics said the Lumina simulation ran on more than 15,000 GPUs and covers a region 1.5 billion light-years across.

briefs.headline: ETH Zurich method records a cell's past gene activity
briefs.summary: Engineered proteins archive several thousand RNA molecules inside living human cells over several days, the team reported in Nature Biotechnology.

briefs.headline: Most US low-risk prostate cancers now go untreated
briefs.summary: Low-risk patients getting neither radiation nor surgery rose from 33.6% to 83.4% in SEER data through 2023, researchers reported in the journal Cancer.

briefs.headline: Nvidia open-sources robot video labeling model Flora
briefs.summary: Nvidia said Flora labels an hour of robot video for about 72 cents against $88.49 for GPT-6 Astra, and scored 57.1% annotation quality to Astra's 53.7%.

briefs.headline: Apollo economist finds no AI payoff outside tech firms
briefs.summary: Torsten Slok, Apollo Global Management's chief economist, said margins and revenue per worker are flat across the S&P 500 excluding seven tech giants.

kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Kyushu banzuke (rankings) is out and the basho opens Nov. 8.
